instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

scenes.title: Cold open
narration: This is Nepalese dance. Ancient to modern.
on_screen: Title card: Nepalese dance · Nepal · Ancient to modern

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Legends attribute the origin of Nepalese dance to the Himalayas, the abode of Lord Shiva and his tandava dance.
Historical records suggest the Maruni dance originated in the 14th century during the time of King Balihang Rana Magar of Palpa, Pokhara, and Butwal.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Dances are performed during religious festivals such as Dashain, Tihar, and the Yenya festival.
Some, like the Kumha Pyakhan and Gathu Pyakhan, are sacred and performed in religious contexts.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Costumes vary by ethnicity and altitude.
In the Jhijhiya dance, women wear earthen pots with fire inside on their heads.
Masked dances like the Lakhey Pyakhan and Gathu Pyakhan utilize traditional masks and are performed in temple and market squares.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Styles include the Newar dances of Kathmandu (e.g., Bhairab Pyakhan), Limbu dances of the east (e.g., Dhan Nach), and Tharu dances of the Terai (e.g., Lathi Nach).

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: Certain dances, such as the Gathu Pyakhan and Kumha Pyakhan, are sacred and restricted; outsiders should respect local customs and restrictions regarding their performance.

music_brief.purpose: original soundtrack faithful to the tradition, with documented commercial reuse rights and no recurring royalties
music_brief.rights_rule: A composition brief does not clear an output. Record the provider/model/version, terms and date, input rights, output licence, restrictions and review before release.
music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Nepalese dance (Nepal). New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

tracks.use: chapters: dance it to the music

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
Traditional public-domain tunes may be used only when the profile names them and a public-domain source is on file; otherwise compose new material in the idiom.
Keep the proportions true: the meter, the tempo range and the instrument roles the sources describe.
Label every generated track with the tool, the date and this brief, so provenance is always clear.
